_comment: Hand-maintained mapping from Eden AI's public model list to pricing.json entries.
Nothing here is inferred at runtime: no fuzzy matching, no lowercasing and hoping.
Eden AI is an AGGREGATOR. The prices below are what Eden charges to forward a call,
which is NOT the price of calling that provider directly: codestral-latest is
$1.00/$3.00 through Eden and $0.30/$0.90 straight from Mistral, both correct, both
published in this file under their own provider. providers.edenai is not a
cross-check of providers.mistral or providers.ovh.
This mapping has a different SHAPE from the other providers', on purpose. Mistral's
and OVH's each name a page element per model -- a card name, a row label, a catalog
id -- because the price sits in a marketing page where a renamed label silently
changes what a figure means. Eden's source is a JSON API stating explicit field
names per model, so there is nothing to string-match and a per-model spec would be
103 copies of the same three lines. What still has to be pinned by a human is the
SET: which upstreams are covered, and exactly which model ids are expected. The
scraper fails if a listed model disappears AND if the upstreams start offering one
that is not listed here -- a price nobody reviewed must never reach the file.
Currency is USD. There is no currency field anywhere in the API. It is confirmed
the same way OVH's EUR was: the endpoint states 0.0000004 per token for
mistral/mistral-medium-2508, and https://app.edenai.run/models renders that exact
model as "$0.40" under a column headed "Input $". If that ever needs revisiting,
it starts here.
Deliberately NOT published, though the API states them:
Tiered prices -- input_cost_per_token_above_128k_tokens (9 models) and the
_above_200k_tokens variants (6 models). A price that depends on how long the
context is has no representation in this schema, and publishing only the first
tier as though it were the price would understate a long-context bill without
ever looking wrong. Left out until the schema can say it properly.
search_context_cost_per_query (10 models) -- a per-query web-search charge, and
itself an object of three sizes (low/medium/high) rather than one figure.
output_cost_per_reasoning_token and citation_cost_per_token (1 model each).
Last verified against the endpoint by a human: 2026-08-10.
